newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES DOWN IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES DOWN IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term interest rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted slightly lower in quiet trade on Monday, with dealers expecting little change in a very liquid market.
"Business is slow and the chances of this changing or the rates moving are very low," one dealer said.
Discount houses were trading treasury bills at 18.60 percent, down on Friday's 17.85 percent with the tender rate unchanged at 18.07 percent.
NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold softer at 19.40 and 18.20 percent respectively from 19.50 and 18.25 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills continued steady at 18.25 percent (buying) and at 17.75 percent (selling). Call money was unchanged at Friday's 18 percent.
